title: Record Retrieval Solutions Pricing 2026
summary: Record Retrieval Solutions charges $45 per request plus provider fees. See what that covers, what it costs to check, and how Codes Health's flat fee compares.
body_markdown:
For plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, and workers' compensation cases, medical record retrieval is a core operational expense that affects case timelines and litigation planning. Understanding how[record retrieval services](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) price their offerings, and what those prices actually include, helps firms budget accurately and avoid surprises.


Pricing in this space varies a lot. Some vendors publish per-request fees while others require custom quotes. Some include AI-powered analysis while others charge separately for chronologies and summaries. And a published base fee rarely tells you the full cost of a case.


This guide looks at Record Retrieval Solutions' published pricing, what drives retrieval costs more broadly, and how to evaluate vendors on total value rather than sticker price alone.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


**RRS publishes its base fee:** Record Retrieval Solutions advertises a $45 retrieval service fee per request, with provider charges and supplemental services billed separately


-


**Compare written quotes:** Check each vendor's billing unit, included services, provider fees, and optional charges before comparing total costs


-


**Base fees don't tell the full story:** An illustrative comparison in American Retrieval's 2024 whitepaper calculates an effective cost of $52.45 against a $44.95 advertised retrieval fee under its stated assumptions


-


**Check additional charges:** Potential additional charges include provider copying fees, document processing, optional analysis, and separately billed requests


-


**Codes Health uses a flat fee model:** Request a written quote confirming the billing unit, included services, provider-fee treatment, and any exclusions


-


**Evaluate speed and completeness together:** An initial delivery may still require follow-up if requested facilities, date ranges, or billing records are missing


## **What Record Retrieval Solutions Charges**


Record Retrieval Solutions publishes a $45 flat fee per request. This establishes the retrieval service fee per request; total case costs depend on the number of requests, provider charges, and optional services.


Here's what to know about how RRS pricing works:


-


**Medical and billing together:** When a provider handles medical and billing records together, they can fall under one request. When billing is handled separately, for example by an outside billing vendor, separate requests and fees may apply


-


**Provider charges:** Provider and copy-service fees may be billed separately. Confirm how the vendor passes through these charges and whether your firm can approve fees above a specified threshold


-


**Supplemental services:** RRS publicly lists supplemental charges and the conditions for separate requests, so review those terms alongside the base fee


-


**Summary service:** RRS's site currently displays a temporary pause notice for its summary service, so confirm availability if you need summaries


-


**Integrations:** Filevine documents an RRS integration, so Filevine users can compare it alongside other options available in their setup


RRS is a straightforward option for firms that want a published per-request retrieval fee and plan to handle analysis separately.


## **Understanding Medical Record Retrieval Service Costs**


Medical record retrieval pricing models fall into several categories, each with different implications for law firm budgets and workflows.


### **Per-Request Pricing**


Per-request pricing charges a set fee for each retrieval request. Examples include:


-


Record Retrieval Solutions advertises a $45 retrieval service fee per request, with provider charges separate


-


Tavrn currently advertises retrieval at $40 per request, excluding provider fees. Confirm current terms when requesting a quote


-


YoCierge's Clio listing advertises pricing starting at $68 per order. Confirm the applicable services and additional charges before comparing quotes


Per-request models carry a few considerations that affect real-world costs:


-


**Separate department requests:** When a provider requires separate requests for medical and billing records, a single case can involve multiple fees


-


**Provider fees passed through:** Provider and copy-service fees may be billed separately


-


**Add-on services:** AI-powered summaries, chronologies, and medical analysis may be separate line items


### **Volume-Based and Subscription Models**


Some vendors offer tiered pricing based on monthly volume or subscription commitments. These models can work for firms with steady retrieval needs, but they add complexity when case volume fluctuates or individual cases require more requests than expected. Ask how overages, unused requests, and contract terms are handled.


### **Flat Fee Models**


Codes Health uses a flat fee model. Request a written quote confirming the billing unit, included retrieval and analysis services, provider-fee treatment, and any exclusions.


When evaluating any flat fee, the useful question is what you get for it: retrieval alone, or retrieval plus chronologies, human-reviewed analysis, and completeness checks.


## **The Value of Transparent Medical Record Retrieval Pricing**


### **Why Pricing Clarity Matters for Legal Practices**


Law firms often work on contingency fees and tight case budgets. Unclear retrieval costs create a few practical problems:


-


**Budget variance:** When actual costs differ from estimates, case cost planning becomes less reliable


-


**Invoice reconciliation overhead:** Reviewing itemized bills with separate charges for retrieval, pages, lookups, and rush processing takes administrative time


-


**Vendor comparison difficulty:** Different pricing structures make side-by-side comparisons harder without written quotes


### **Additional Costs to Check**


American Retrieval's 2024 whitepaper walks through how base pricing can differ from actual costs. Potential additional charges include provider copying fees, document processing, optional analysis, and separately billed requests. Ask which charges apply and whether any page thresholds affect the quote. Items worth asking about include:


-


Bates stamping


-


Facility address lookups


-


Scanning large records


-


Highlighting and annotating


-


Extra document requests, such as death certificates or imaging CDs


-


"No records found" responses


The whitepaper compares two hypothetical vendors across 1,000 requests. In that illustrative scenario, Company A advertised $30 per retrieval and averaged $27.75 after accounting for reduced charges on "no records" responses. Company B advertised $44.95 and averaged $52.45 once additional fees were included.


For that example, Company B's effective cost came in roughly 17% above its advertised rate. It's an illustration under stated assumptions, not a general benchmark, but it's a good reminder to compare complete fee schedules. Actual costs depend on the fee schedule, provider charges, and services required.


### **Measuring ROI in Record Retrieval**


Return on investment goes beyond per-request pricing:


-


**Time saved:** How much paralegal time does the vendor save through tracking, provider follow-up, and organized delivery?


-


**Completeness:** Do records arrive complete, or do follow-up requests add cycles and costs?


-


**Analysis value:** Does the vendor provide insights such as potential care issues, missing record detection, and documented future treatment needs, or just files?


-


**Integration efficiency:** Can the firm work within its existing case management system?


## **Codes Health: A Premier Solution for Medical Record Retrieval**


Codes Health is an AI-powered medical record retrieval and analysis platform built for plaintiff law firms. Founded in 2024 by MIT and Yale graduates and backed by investors including Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Amplify Partners, and Haystack, the platform pairs retrieval with analysis.


### **What Codes Health Offers**


Codes Health uses a flat fee model. Request a written quote confirming the billing unit, included retrieval and analysis services, provider-fee treatment, and any exclusions. Its documented capabilities include:


-


Medical record retrieval through custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone outreach


-


AI-powered case chronology generation


-


Human review of AI-generated insights


-


Completeness checks before delivery


-


Potential care concerns flagged for attorney review


-


Documented future treatment needs surfaced for review


-


Authorization validation before submission


### **Evaluating Speed and Completeness Together**


Some vendors emphasize speed, with same-day or 24-hour retrieval. Evaluate advertised speed alongside record scope and completeness. An initial delivery may still require follow-up if requested facilities, date ranges, or billing records are missing.


Codes Health's position is that services promising same-day retrieval often don't get the complete record set and need extra client involvement to fill the gaps, which can contribute to client churn. Codes Health describes retrieval taking a couple of weeks and checks delivered batches for completeness, so firms get complete records in weeks, not months.


### **AI Analysis With Human Review**


General AI tools like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review. Codes Health's purpose-built platform uses a workflow that combines automated analysis with human review of AI-generated insights.


That matters because AI alone can miss context, misread abbreviations, or flag false positives. Human review helps identify errors and contextual issues before the firm relies on the analysis.

### **Embedded Workflow Benefits**


Instead of managing retrieval through a separate vendor portal, Filevine users can:


-

-

-


Track request status and provider outreach in real time


-

-

This embedded approach reduces context switching between case management, email, vendor portals, and downloaded file folders.


### **Authorization Validation Before Submission**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can cause providers to reject requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or missing consent for sensitive records can lead to correction and resubmission.


Within the Filevine workflow, Codes Health's AI reviews authorizations before submission, flagging:


-


Misspellings in patient names or provider information


-


Missing dates of service


-


Signature problems


-


Incomplete authorization forms


-


Provider-specific requirements


Pre-submission checks help identify authorization errors that could otherwise lead to rejection, correction, and resubmission.


## **The Cost-Benefit of AI-Powered Medical Record Analysis**


Retrieval delivers files. Analysis helps legal teams use them. The cost difference shows up beyond the invoice.


### **Time Savings Through Automated Chronologies**


Manually organizing thousands of pages into chronological order takes significant paralegal time. AI-powered chronologies organize and compile records automatically, grouping patient encounters and bills by visit.


To estimate labor savings, compare manual preparation time with AI-assisted preparation and review time. Multiply the difference by case volume, then assess whether the recovered capacity reduces overtime or supports additional work.


### **Insights That Affect Case Strategy**


Beyond organization, Codes Health's analysis tools surface information relevant to case strategy:


-


**Diagnoses and treatments:** Structured extraction from unstructured records


-


**Pre-existing conditions:** Prior injuries relevant to causation arguments


-


**Missed appointments:** Care gaps that may affect damages claims


-


**Future treatment needs:** Documented future treatment needs for review in damages analysis


-


**Potential care concerns:** AI surfaces potential care concerns for evaluation by the legal team and qualified medical experts


These insights would otherwise require attorney or nurse paralegal review of every page. AI can surface them, and human review helps confirm them.


### **Missing Record Detection**


Incomplete delivery is an easy cost factor to overlook. When records arrive missing key date ranges, facilities, or billing documentation, firms can face:


-


Delayed case progression while requesting additional records


-


Surprises when missing records surface during discovery


-


Documentation gaps that create uncertainty in negotiations


Codes Health's completeness review compares delivered materials against the original request and available patient history, identifying gaps before the record set is treated as complete.


## **Choosing the Right Record Retrieval Partner: Beyond the Price Tag**


Choosing a retrieval vendor on per-request price alone leaves out factors that affect total cost of ownership.


### **Key Evaluation Criteria**


When comparing vendors, consider:


-


**Pricing structure:** Per-request, subscription, or flat fee? What's included versus extra?


-


**Provider fee handling:** Passed through at cost, included, or marked up?


-


**Turnaround time:** Does the stated average reflect complete delivery or just the first delivery?


-


**Completeness checks:** Does the vendor check for gaps before delivery?


-


**AI capabilities:** Included, available as an add-on, or not offered?


-


**Human review:** Who reviews AI outputs, and what are their qualifications?


-


**Integration options:** Does the service work within your case management system?


-


**Privacy and security:** Review the vendor's safeguards, access controls, and applicable contractual responsibilities for handling sensitive records


### **The Total Cost Equation**


Compare written quotes using the same case mix, request count, record scope, and analysis requirements. Calculate retrieval service fees, provider charges, optional services, and internal follow-up costs separately. For Codes Health, confirm the flat fee's scope and exclusions before comparing totals.

Codes Health tailors its insights to specific case types rather than generating generic summaries.


### **Integration Capabilities**


Codes Health's Filevine integration brings retrieval workflows into the firm's case management environment. Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and medical software for high-volume customers, subject to project scope.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.


## **Optimizing Medical Record Retrieval: A Strategic Investment**


Treating retrieval purely as a transactional expense to minimize per request can miss the value that complete, analyzed records provide.


Strong medical documentation supports:


-


Case qualification decisions


-


Damages analysis


-


Settlement preparation


-


Trial preparation


-


Fewer discovery surprises


Evaluate potential workflow benefits alongside retrieval fees when assessing total case costs.


## **Bottom Line: Looking Beyond the Per-Request Fee**


Most retrieval budget problems are preventable. They come from comparing base fees without the full fee schedule, overlooking separate requests and provider charges, sending authorizations no one checked, and treating a first delivery as a complete record set.


Record Retrieval Solutions offers a clear, published $45 retrieval fee per request, with provider charges and supplemental services billed separately, which suits firms that want retrieval only and handle analysis elsewhere. Firms that want retrieval, pre-submission validation, completeness checks, and human-reviewed analysis from one partner can look at Codes Health's flat fee model, typically delivering complete records in a couple of weeks.


[Request a demo](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) to see how Codes Health's retrieval and analysis work for your case volume, and get a written quote confirming what the flat fee covers.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How does Codes Health's flat-fee pricing compare to per-request models?**


Codes Health uses a flat fee model, while vendors like Record Retrieval Solutions charge a published fee per request with provider charges separate. Request a written quote from Codes Health confirming the billing unit, included retrieval and analysis services, provider-fee treatment, and any exclusions, then compare totals using the same case assumptions.


### **What causes retrieval costs to exceed initial quotes?**


Common factors include separate requests when medical and billing records are handled by different departments, provider copy fees passed through at cost, page-based charges, lookup fees, and add-on services for chronologies or summaries. Actual costs depend on the fee schedule, provider charges, and services required.


### **How does authorization validation affect retrieval costs?**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can cause providers to reject requests, and each correction takes paralegal time. Codes Health's AI reviews authorizations before submission. ### **Why should firms evaluate completeness alongside retrieval speed?**
